$comment: Built-in list prices in micro-USD per million tokens (1 USD = 1_000_000 micro-USD).
This is the BASELINE layer — the floor. Effective pricing is resolved as:
1. this document — always present, never fails to load, no network, no credentials
2. the last fetch that succeeded (mvp/pricing_feeds/snapshot.py, in DynamoDB)
3. the active price source (STRATOCLAVE_PRICE_SOURCE; "json" reads this file,
"bedrock-live" reads mvp/pricing_feeds — see docs/design/price-feeds.md)
4. admin overrides in the PricingConfig table — highest precedence
Every number below was MEASURED against the provider's own APIs on 2026-08-31 and
is the IN-REGION (geo / Regional-CRIS) standard-tier rate, because every registry
entry addresses its model through a `us.` inference profile and that is what such a
request is billed at. The cheaper `global` rate is 10% lower and is NOT the floor:
the floor's job is to be safe when a feed is unavailable, and safe means it does not
under-charge. Sources: bedrock:ListFoundationModelAgreementOffers for the
Marketplace-metered families (Anthropic, OpenAI GPT-5.x) and the Price List API's
AmazonBedrock / AmazonBedrockFoundationModels offers for the rest.
A key absent from every layer falls back to "default", which is Opus-priced:
an unpriced model must over-charge, never under-charge.
Models reference a key via `pricing_key` in defaults/models.json. A key is a PRICE
POINT, not a family: Opus 4.1 lists at three times Opus 5, so they cannot share one
(a shared key is charged at its dearest member). `price_feed_key_spans_prices` fires
when a live fetch finds a key whose models disagree.
A rate object may also carry `notes`; any other key is rejected as a typo.

opus.notes: Claude Opus 4.5 / 4.6 / 4.7 / 4.8 / 5 — $5.50/$27.50 per MTok in-region ($5.00/$25.00 global). Measured 2026-08-31.

opus-legacy.notes: Claude Opus 4, Opus 4.1 and Claude 3 Opus — $15/$75 per MTok, with no global variant. Split out of "opus" because a key is charged at its dearest member and these three are three times the current tier.

fable.notes: Claude Fable 5 — $11/$55 per MTok in-region ($10/$50 global), above the Opus tier. Measured 2026-08-31.

sonnet.notes: Claude Sonnet 4 / 4.5 / 4.6 — $3.30/$16.50 per MTok in-region ($3.00/$15.00 global). Measured 2026-08-31. Sonnet 5 is NOT in this tier: it lists lower and carries "sonnet-5".

sonnet-5.notes: Claude Sonnet 5 — $2.20/$11.00 per MTok in-region ($2.00/$10.00 global), which is CHEAPER than Sonnet 4.5/4.6. Found by the live feed's key-spread check on its first real run: while it shared the "sonnet" key it was charged at $3.30/$16.50, 50% over its own rate.

sonnet-3.notes: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude 3 Sonnet — $3/$15 per MTok, published with no in-region premium.

haiku.notes: Claude Haiku 4.5 — $1.10/$5.50 per MTok in-region ($1.00/$5.00 global). Measured 2026-08-31.

haiku-3-5.notes: Claude 3.5 Haiku — $0.80/$4.00 per MTok. The Latency Optimized variant is a separate product at $1.00/$5.00 and is not served, so it is not the floor here.

haiku-3.notes: Claude 3 Haiku — $0.25/$1.25 per MTok. It does not support prompt caching and Bedrock publishes no cache rate for it, so the cache legs are an UPPER BOUND (read = input, write = 1.25x input) rather than a published price.

gpt-5.notes: Generic GPT-5.x key, kept for an entry that names no specific tier. Priced at the dearest measured GPT-5.6 tier (sol) so it cannot under-charge a cheaper one.

gpt-5.6-sol.notes: $5.50/$33.00 per MTok in-region ($5.00/$30.00 global), cache read $0.55, cache write $6.875. Measured 2026-08-31 from the model's own agreement rate card, which corrected the $4.40/$22.00 figure this row previously carried from a model-card reading.

gpt-5.6-terra.notes: $2.20/$13.20 per MTok in-region, cache read $0.275, cache write $3.4375. Measured 2026-08-31.

grok.notes: xAI Grok 4.6 — $2.20/$6.60 per MTok in-region, cache read $0.55. Bedrock publishes no cache-WRITE rate; the 1.25x-input premium the Anthropic tiers use is assumed as an UPPER BOUND so the ledger never under-charges.

gemma.notes: Gemma 4 31B — $0.14/$0.40 per MTok standard tier in the AmazonBedrock offer (measured 2026-08-31). No cache rate is published, so the cache legs are an upper bound (read = input, write = 1.25x input). This row previously defaulted to the Opus tier, which over-charged by ~35x.

nemotron.notes: NVIDIA Nemotron Super 3 120B — $0.15/$0.65 per MTok standard tier (measured 2026-08-31). Cache legs are an upper bound for the same reason as gemma.

qwen.notes: Qwen3 Next 80B A3B — $0.14/$1.20 per MTok standard tier (measured 2026-08-31; billed under the id qwen.qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct). Cache legs are an upper bound for the same reason as gemma.

vllm.notes: Self-hosted capacity. This is a cost-recovery rate the operator sets, not a list price; the cache legs MUST stay zero because vLLM reports no Bedrock-style cache split. STRATOCLAVE_SELFHOSTED_RATES_PATH lets a deployment publish its own figure through the same feed pipeline.

default.notes: The fallback for a pricing key that exists nowhere, which in practice means a typo. It DOMINATES every provider row in this document, leg by leg (the dearest is the legacy Opus tier at $15/$75), because the stated rule is that an unpriced model over-charges rather than under-charges — and a fallback that is cheaper than a real tier breaks exactly that rule for the models that tier covers. test_pricing_floor.py enforces the domination.
